cards.title: Presidential ordinance withdraws most privileges of KP MPAs, including protection against preventive detention
cards.author: Waseem Ahmad Shah
cards.why: This is a significant constitutional and governance development involving the suspension of provincial legislative privileges, which is highly relevant to exams on the Pakistani political system.
cards.summary: President Asif Ali Zardari has issued five ordinances to curtail the powers and privileges of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) lawmakers. Key changes include removing protections against preventive detention and establishing executive committees to manage development schemes in the province. These measures follow the imposition of emergency rule in KP last October.
key_facts: President Zardari promulgated five ordinances affecting KP governance on November 19, 2026.
The ordinances remove protections against preventive detention for KP MPAs.
New executive committees will have powers to oversee special initiatives and developmental schemes in 12 security-challenged districts.
The ordinances include amendments to the KP Provincial Assembly (Powers, Immunities and Privileges) Act 2026.

vocab.meaning: Put a law or ordinance into effect by official proclamation.
Imprisonment of a person without trial, typically to prevent them from committing a future crime.

text: PESHAWAR: President Asif Ali Zardari has promulgated five ordinances, doing away with most of the “privileges” of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa lawmakers, including protection against “preventive detention” and providing a legal framework for special initiatives in the designated 12 districts and other districts in the province.

With the imposition of emergency in KP on Oct 11, an Area Representative and Development Council (ARDC) was formed to oversee 12 districts that were deemed to face intense security challenges, including the merged districts.

Two of the ordinances envisage setting up an executive committee with wide-ranging powers to oversee special initiatives, including developmental schemes, in the 12 designated districts and the rest of the province, respectively.
The committee will have powers to identify and recommend the executing agency for special initiatives in the designated and other districts, including military formations.

In a statement on Saturday, President Zardari’s office confirmed he had promulgated five ordinances pertaining to KP. Of these, the following four had been published in the Official Gazette on Nov 19 after their promulgation:
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Societies (Registration) (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026;
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Special Initiative Ordinance, 2026 (specific districts);
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Special Initiative Ordinance, 2026 (other districts);
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Provincial Assembly (Powers, Immunities and Privileges) Ordinance, 2026 (XI of 2026).
The fifth was the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Speaker and Deputy Speaker (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Ordinance 2026.

Through the amendment ordinance related to privileges of MPAs, drastic changes have been made in the KP Provincial Assembly (Powers, Immunities and Privileges) Act 2026, as 21 of its 40 sections have been omitted, including those providing protection to the MPAs against “preventive detentions” and offences related to “breach” of privileges.
The schedule of offences related to “breach of privileges” of the Assembly, its members and committees has also been omitted, thus leaving them without significant privileges.

It may be mentioned that Sohail Afridi — whose role as the chief minister was rendered non-functional due to governor’s rule — Speaker Babar Saleem Swati and other lawmakers have been in “ preventive detention ” since emergency was imposed, according to police.
KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi also said last month that they had been placed under house arrest .

The important provisions omitted through the ordinance include sections 5 (attendance of MPA detained or arrested), 6 (members not liable to civil or criminal action), 10 (preventive detention), 11 (permission of speaker before arrest, detention, etc. of a member), 15 (power to summon), 22 (power to arrest), 31 (breach of privilege), 32 (breach of privilege to be an offence) and 34 (cognisance of offence).
Special initiative ordinances
The two ordinances relate to special initiatives in the 12 designated districts and the remaining districts in the province, respectively.

Both the ordinances provide for the establishment of an executive committee comprising a chairman, vice chairman and other such members as nominated by the prime minister, in case of designated district, and by the governor of the province, in case of the remaining districts.

For the designated districts, the Area Development Secretariat shall serve as secretariat of the executive committee, whereas for the other districts, the planning and development department shall serve as the secretariat of the committee.

Under the new laws, “special initiative” includes any work, developmental scheme, rehabilitation or reconstruction work, procurement of goods and human resources, consulting or non-consulting services or any other activity involving expenditure of public funds as determined by the executive committee.
The executive committee, in both the ordinances, has extensive powers including:
Identify an initiative as a special initiative of urgent or emergent nature;
Scrutinise and approve proposals, concept papers and PC-Is for the special initiatives;
Grant anticipatory approval for the initiatives, proposals, concept papers and PC-Is of the special initiatives;
Identify and recommend the executing agency, including military organisations and formations, for the execution of the special initiatives;
Provide a mechanism for the monitoring and evaluation of the special initiatives, including third-party monitoring and evaluation;
Review progress of the special initiatives;
Constitute committees or designate persons to carry out functions assigned to them by the executive committee;
Perform any other act to carry out the purposes of the ordinance.
The ordinances provide that the executive committee should meet at least once a month or as and when required.
The decisions of the committee shall be made on the basis of majority vote of its members, and in case of a tie, the chairman shall have the casting vote.
The chairman is also empowered to co-opt any other member or technical expert, to offer advice to the committee, as required.
Both the ordinances have overriding effect on other laws, including the KP Public Procurement Regulatory Authority Act 2012 and the KP Public Private Partnership Act 2020.
Moreover, no civil court shall have jurisdiction in relation to an act done, order passed, and any proceedings done under the ordinances.
Madressah registrations
Through the KP Societies (Registration) (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026, a sub-section 1-A has been included in Section 21, dealing with the registration of “religious madressahs”.

The newly included provision provides that madressahs which are or may be registered with the Directorate General of Religious Education, Ministry of Federal Education and Professional Training, shall not be required to be registered under the Act (Societies Registration Act).

cards.title: At SCO moot in India, Musadik Malik declares climate change ‘enemy’ of civilisations
cards.author: News Desk
cards.why: The story bridges climate change, international diplomacy, and regional cooperation, all of which are essential topics for Current Affairs and International Relations.
cards.summary: Pakistan’s Climate Change Minister, Musadik Malik, attended the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum in India. He identified climate change as an existential threat to civilizations and cited the 2022 floods in Pakistan as a catastrophic example. This visit marks the first by a Pakistani minister to India since May 2023.
key_facts: Climate Change Minister Musadik Malik visited New Delhi for the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum.
This is the first visit by a Pakistani minister to India since Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari's visit in May 2023.
The 2022 monsoon floods in Pakistan killed 1,700 people and submerged one-third of the country.
The minister noted that recent floods damaged the ancient site of Mohenjo-Daro.

vocab.meaning: Cooperation among several countries to address common issues.

text: Climate Change Minister Musadik Malik on Saturday declared climate change an “enemy” of civilisations as he highlighted its impact on South Asian countries at a meeting of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) in India.

Malik is in New Delhi on a three-day trip to attend the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum, making him the first Pakistani minister to visit the neighbour since former foreign minister Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari attended an SCO meeting in May 2023.
Addressing the forum on Saturday, the minister said the enemy of this civilisation was not another civilisation but climate change, noting that Nepal’s representative also spoke about the issue.
Malik recalled the Aug 26 floods in Nepal, which claimed over 1,400 lives and left thousands of others missing, as well as the devastating 2022 floods in Pakistan.
He noted that those monsoon floods left 1,700 people dead and submerged one-third of the country, including almost the entire Sindh.
“Four days of rain caused Mohenjo Daro’s walls to fall; those walls that no one was able to break for 4,500 years, climate [change] and rain-induced floods did it.”
The minister remarked that humans were also an “enemy”, as they contributed to climate destruction.
“Do you know what is the meaning of Mohenjo-Daro?” Malik asked. “It means mound of the dead.”
Malik said the ancient site had, in a sense, opened its gates to the living during the 2022 floods, providing refuge to people displaced by the disaster.

He said people had sought shelter wherever they could find it, including parking lots and shopping malls, while mosques, temples, shrines and schools in Balochistan had also opened their doors to those affected by the floods.
“This is the power of civilisation. This is the power through which nations survive,” the minister noted.

During his speech, Malik presented three proposals for SCO, including the establishment of a network of cultural institutions, a digital repository to present the region’s historical and natural “gifts” to the world, and a climate-resilient heritage framework to address destruction caused by climate change in the region.

At the outset of his address, Malik said he had initially intended to deliver his speech in English but felt more inclined to speak in Urdu after considering his proximity to the tombs of Urdu poet Mirza Ghalib and Sufi saint Nizamuddin.
“It felt a little strange to speak in English. So, with your permission, I would like to speak in Urdu,” he said.
The minister pointed out that distinct identities were needed for dialogue, which could only take place between diverse voices.

“If there is one identity, one voice, then a monologue is needed. There is no need for dialogue,” he said, comparing it to waking up in the morning, looking in the mirror and speaking only to oneself.
“There is no beauty in that. Beauty is [in] the vase that has colourful flowers, the smell of different kinds. Today, we’re here to celebrate that colourful vase,” the minister said.

During his address, the minister highlighted Pakistan’s history and how its civilisation had been shaped by multiple influences, with connections extending across China, Central Asia, Iran and the Middle East.

“When we look at our history, all our roads lead to the north; Bukhara and Samarkand and Central Asia and Afghanistan. The entire history takes us to the north,” he said. “And when we talk about our prayers, our poetry, we are drawn towards the Middle East and Iran or Persia.”
Malik said diversity and the free flow of ideas and identities were something to be embraced. “There is wisdom there, in embracing it. We’re here to celebrate these things today.”
Meetings with Indian minister, others
Dr Malik arrived at Purana Qila in New Delhi for the second day of the inaugural SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum, according to a post shared by his office earlier in the day.
On the sidelines of the forum, Malik held separate bilateral meetings with representatives from various countries, including host India, Nepal, Iran and Tajikistan.
He met with Indian Minister for Culture and Tourism Gajendra Singh Shekhawat and Indian Secretary for Culture Vivek Aggarwal, state-run APP reported.

According to APP , the discussions focused on cultural ties and opportunities for promoting cooperation between Pakistan and India, with both sides exchanging views on matters of mutual interest and the importance of strengthening cultural and civilisational links.
During his meeting with Nepal’s Culture and Tourism Minister Khadga Raj Poudel, the climate change minister expressed deep grief over the loss of precious human lives in the August floods.
Malik emphasised that urgent global action was essential to address the growing risks of natural disasters caused by climate change.

In his meeting with Tajikistan’s Minister of Culture Sattoriyon Amonzoda, Malik underscored the strong historical and cultural ties between the two countries, the Pakistan High Commission in India said.
He reaffirmed Pakistan’s resolve to further strengthen these multifaceted ties, particularly through greater people-to-people exchanges.

In a separate meeting with the president of Iran’s Islamic Culture and Relations Organisation, Mohammad Mahdi Imanipour, Dr Malik underscored the deep-rooted historical and cultural bonds between Pakistan and Iran.
He reaffirmed Pakistan’s firm commitment to further expanding these fraternal ties across all spheres, the high commission said.
Meanwhile, Malik and Azerbaijan’s Culture Minister Adil Karimli expressed their commitment to further strengthening the long-standing fraternal ties between Islamabad and Baku.
Malik emphasised the need to enhance cooperation across all sectors of the bilateral relationship between the two countries.
The climate change minister also met with Kyrgyz Republic’s Deputy Minister of Culture and Youth Policy Askaraly Shukuralievich.

A day earlier, after arriving in New Delhi, Malik had described the forum as a “tremendous opportunity” for multilateral dialogue, saying that cultures and civilisations transcended geographical boundaries.
Speaking to Indian news agency ANI , he had said the gathering offered an opportunity to discuss shared history, geography, cultures and civilisations.
Malik’s India trip comes two years after India’s External Affairs Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar visited Islamabad for an SCO meeting.
Pakistan currently holds the rotating chairmanship of the SCO Council of Heads of State for the 2026-27 term and is scheduled to host the organisation’s summit in Islamabad in August 2027.

cards.title: US court hands Indian national Nikhil Gupta 20 years for Sikh murder plot
cards.author: Anwar Iqbal
cards.why: This case involves sensitive international relations, intelligence operations, and transnational legal issues that impact regional security analysis.
cards.summary: A US court sentenced Indian national Nikhil Gupta to nearly 20 years in prison for his role in a plot to assassinate a Sikh activist in the United States. Prosecutors stated the plot was directed by an Indian government official linked to the Research and Analysis Wing (RAW). The foiled assassination targeted an activist advocating for an independent state called Khalistan.
key_facts: Nikhil Gupta was sentenced to 235 months in prison for murder-for-hire and conspiracy charges.
The plot targeted Gurpatwant Singh Pannun, a US-based Sikh nationalist leader.
US prosecutors alleged the operation was directed by an Indian government official.
Gupta arranged a $15,000 advance payment to an undercover US law enforcement officer posing as a hitman.

vocab.meaning: The murder of a prominent person, often for political reasons.
A secret plan by a group to do something unlawful.

text: WASHINGTON: An Indian national has been sentenced to 235 months in prison for his role in a plot allegedly directed by an Indian government official to assassinate a US-based Sikh nationalist leader on American soil, the US Department of Justice (DOJ) announced on Friday.

Nikhil Gupta, 55, also known as Nick, was sentenced by US District Judge Victor Marrero in the Southern District of New York after pleading guilty in February 2026 to murder-for-hire, conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire and conspiracy to commit money laundering.

The case involved an alleged conspiracy to kill Gurpatwant Singh Pannun , a US and Canadian citizen, attorney and political activist who advocates the creation of an independent Sikh homeland, Khalistan, in India.

According to the DOJ, Gupta worked with Vikash Yadav, a co-defendant and Indian government employee, to organise the 2023 assassination. Yadav was employed by India’s cabinet secretariat that houses the country’s foreign intelligence service, the Research and Analysis Wing (RAW).

Additional details emerging from the court proceedings indicate that Gupta arranged a $15,000 advance payment to a person he believed was a hired assassin. The individual was actually an undercover US law enforcement officer.
Gupta and Yadav had discussed paying $100,000 for the assassination. Gupta also supplied information about Pannun to the supposed hitman to facilitate the killing.

Prosecutors said Yadav provided personal data of Pannun, including his home address, phone numbers and details of his daily movements. Gupta allegedly passed this information to the undercover operative and kept Yadav informed about the progress of the operation.
The plot was foiled by US agencies before Pannun could be killed.
Prosecution sought 24 years

Prosecutors had sought 293 months, citing his alleged role in a foreign-directed plot to assassinate Pannun, while the defence requested 144 months, citing his lack of a criminal record, alcohol dependence and personal circumstances.
During the hearing, Gupta apologised to Pannun, affected communities and his family, expressing regret for abandoning Mahatma Gandhi’s principle of non-violence.
Pannun thanked US authorities for prosecuting the case and reaffirmed his commitment to Sikh independence.
The case has also been linked to the June 2023 killing of Sikh nationalist leader Hardeep Singh Nijjar in Canada, though Gupta’s defence denied his involvement in Nijjar’s assassination.

Prosecutors had identified Indian official Yadav as the alleged director of the operation. He remains in India despite a US arrest warrant issued in October 2024, as India denies role in assassination plots.
Published in Dawn, November 21st, 2026
